newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow at mostly $62-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow at mostly $62-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Panhandle feedlot cattle sales Tuesday were slow and mostly at $62.00 per cwt, unchanged from Monday's active trade, but down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 2,500 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 3,500 in Kansas, they said.
There also were thin sales reported at $61.00 for lighter weight cattle that would likely grade less than those traded at $62.00 earlier, the sources said.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by sluggish beef demand, which also weighed on beef prices, they said.

Fed prices also were lower amid a need for feedlots to remain current even if owners were losing money at current prices, feedlot sources said. Cattle supplies were larger than a week ago and were expected to expand further through July, they said. At $62.00, the average loss for cattle owners was about $50.00 per head, several feedlot sources said.
"What we need to do is unhook them and get them out of here because there's a lot of cattle on the way," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
"We need to try to stay current and hope that prices will come back in August," he said.
Cattle supplies were seen lighter in August, sources said.
